questions.stem: A rare whisky barrel sold for \(\$18{,}700\) after a price rise of \(15\%\). What was the original price before the rise? Round to the nearest cent.

steps.explain: We are given the price AFTER a 15% increase and need to find the price BEFORE. This is a reverse-percentage problem. If the original price is \(P\), then \(P \times 1.15 = 18700\). We isolate \(P\) by dividing both sides by 1.15.
Perform the division to find the original price.
The original price of the whisky barrel was \(\\(16{,}260.87\). This confirms the 15% increase: \(16260.87 \times 1.15 \approx 18700\).\)

questions.stem: A pharmaceutical wholesaler sells antibiotics to a clinic for \(\$4{,}560\) including \(14\%\) GST. What is the pre-GST price? Round to the nearest cent.

steps.explain: The GST-inclusive price means the original price has been multiplied by \(1.14\). To reverse this and find the pre-GST price, we divide the total by \(1.14\).
Carry out the division.
The pre-GST price is \(\\(4{,}000.00\). Verification: \(4000 \times 1.14 = 4560\) ✓.\)

questions.stem: A mining company's weekly ore output fell from \(8{,}400\) tonnes to \(7{,}098\) tonnes during a wet season. What is the percentage decrease? Round to two decimal places.

steps.explain: The percentage decrease is calculated by finding how much the value dropped relative to the original value. Formula: \(\%\, text{decrease} = \dfrac{\text{original} - \text{new}}{\text{original}} \times 100\).
Calculate the numerator (the drop in output).
Divide the drop by the original and multiply by 100.
The ore output decreased by \(15.50\%\) during the wet season.

questions.stem: A commercial bakery's monthly flour cost rose by \(8\%\) in January, then fell by \(5\%\) in February. If the original monthly cost was \(\$3{,}200\), what is the final cost after both changes? Round to the nearest cent.

steps.explain: We apply two successive percentage changes to the original cost. Each change is applied to the result of the previous step, not to the original. First, apply the \(8\%\) increase in January.
Now apply the \(5\%\) decrease in February to the new cost \(V_1\).
Compute the final cost.
The final monthly flour cost is \(\\(3{,}283.20\). Note this is not simply \(8\% - 5\% = 3\%\) increase on original; compound changes differ from simple addition.\)

questions.stem: A yacht broker purchased a sailing vessel and sold it for \(\$312{,}000\), making a profit of \(20\%\). What did the broker originally pay for the yacht?

steps.explain: The selling price represents the cost price plus a \(20\%\) profit. So the selling price is \(120\%\) of the cost price. We divide the selling price by \(1.20\) to recover the original cost.
Perform the division.
The broker originally paid \(\\(260{,}000\). Check: \(260000 \times 1.20 = 312000\) ✓.\)

questions.stem: A renewable energy firm installs solar panels at a base cost of \(\$42{,}000\). The installer adds a \(12\%\) labour charge, then the government applies a \(10\%\) GST to the total. What is the final amount the customer pays? Round to the nearest cent.

steps.explain: First apply the \(12\%\) labour charge to the base cost to find the pre-GST total.
Now apply \(10\%\) GST to \(V_1\) to get the final customer price.
Calculate the final amount.
The customer pays \(\\(51{,}744.00\) in total after the labour charge and GST are applied.\)

questions.stem: A wildlife survey estimated a koala colony at \(480\) individuals. A follow-up census recorded \(552\). What is the percentage increase in population? Round to two decimal places.

steps.explain: Percentage increase = \(\dfrac{\text{new} - \text{original}}{\text{original}} \times 100\). We use the original value (480) as the denominator since the increase is measured relative to where we started.
Find the difference.
Divide by the original and multiply by 100.
The koala population increased by \(15.00\%\).

questions.stem: A cafe bought coffee beans for \(\$18\) per kilogram and sold them brewed at an effective price of \(\$27\) per kilogram equivalent. What percentage profit did the cafe make?

steps.explain: Profit percentage is calculated on the cost price (buying price). Formula: \(\%\, mathrm{profit} = \dfrac{\mathrm{selling\ price} - \mathrm{cost\ price}}{\mathrm{cost\ price}} \times 100\).
Calculate the numerator.
Divide by cost and multiply by 100.
The cafe made a \(50\%\) profit on the coffee beans. Note: This is profit on cost, not on selling price.

questions.stem: A data analytics firm recorded \(1{,}250\) server errors in Q1 and \(875\) in Q2. By what percentage did the error count decrease from Q1 to Q2?

steps.explain: Percentage decrease = \(\dfrac{\mathrm{original} - \mathrm{new}}{\mathrm{original}} \times 100\). The original is the Q1 count.
Find the reduction.
Divide and multiply.
Server errors fell by \(30.00\%\) from Q1 to Q2.

questions.stem: A surfboard retailer marks up wholesale boards by \(35\%\), then offers a loyalty card discount of \(8\%\). If the wholesale cost is \(\$640\), what is the loyalty card price? Round to the nearest cent.

steps.explain: Apply the \(35\%\) markup to the wholesale cost to get the retail price.
Apply the \(8\%\) loyalty discount to the retail price.
Compute the final loyalty price.
The loyalty card price is \(\\(793.92\).\)

questions.stem: A laboratory measured a chemical sample at \(47.3\) g. The actual mass was \(50.0\) g. What is the percentage error in the measurement? Round to two decimal places.

steps.explain: Percentage error = \(\dfrac{|\mathrm{measured} - \mathrm{actual}|}{\mathrm{actual}} \times 100\). We always use the actual (true) value as the denominator.
Find the absolute difference.
Divide by the actual value and multiply by 100.
The percentage error is \(5.40\%\). A smaller percentage error indicates a more accurate measurement.

questions.stem: A fitness equipment distributor sells treadmills at a \(40\%\) profit on cost. If the selling price is \(\$2{,}100\), find the cost price.

steps.explain: A \(40\%\) profit on cost means the selling price is \(140\%\) of the cost price. So: \(\mathrm{cost} \times 1.40 = 2100\). Divide both sides by \(1.40\).
Perform the division.

questions.stem: A sports club's membership fee increased by \(6\%\) in 2023 and by another \(4\%\) in 2024. What is the overall percentage increase over the two years? Round to two decimal places.

steps.explain: Two successive percentage increases are NOT simply added. The combined multiplier is \(1.06 \times 1.04\). We apply this to a reference value of \(1\) (or \(100\)) and find the overall change.
Compute the combined multiplier.
Convert to percentage increase: subtract 1 and multiply by 100.
The overall increase is \(10.24\%\), which is slightly more than \(10\%\) due to the compounding effect of applying the second increase to the already-increased price.

questions.stem: A property developer sold an apartment for \(\$875{,}000\), which was \(25\%\) more than the purchase price. How much did the developer originally pay for the apartment?

steps.explain: The selling price is \(125\%\) of the purchase price. Set up the equation: \(\mathrm{purchase} \times 1.25 = 875000\), then divide both sides by \(1.25\).
Compute the purchase price.
The developer originally paid \(\\(700{,}000\). Verify: \(700000 \times 1.25 = 875000\) ✓.\)

questions.stem: A fishing trawler's catch dropped by \(18\%\) in summer and then fell a further \(12\%\) in autumn. What is the overall percentage decrease from the original catch? Round to two decimal places.

steps.explain: Two successive decreases combine multiplicatively. The remaining fraction after both decreases is \((1 - 0.18) \times (1 - 0.12)\).
Multiply the two factors.
The overall percentage decrease is \(1 - 0.7216 = 0.2784\), expressed as a percentage.
The trawler's catch fell by \(27.84\%\) overall — less than the sum \(18\%+12\%=30\%\) because the second decrease acts on the already-reduced amount.

questions.stem: A horticultural nursery priced rare orchids at \(\$380\) each, then discounted them by \(20\%\). After the sale, what percentage of the original price was the discounted price?

steps.explain: A \(20\%\) discount means the customer pays \(100\% - 20\% = 80\%\) of the original price. We can verify by computing the discounted price and expressing it as a fraction of the original.
Express the discounted price as a percentage of original.
The discounted price is \(80\%\) of the original. This directly follows from the definition: removing \(20\%\) leaves \(80\%\).

questions.stem: A telecommunications tower upgrade cost \(\$560{,}000\) excluding GST. After adding \(10\%\) GST and a \(5\%\) council levy on the GST-inclusive amount, what is the total cost? Round to the nearest dollar.

steps.explain: First add \(10\%\) GST to the base cost.
Then apply the \(5\%\) council levy to the GST-inclusive amount.
Compute the final total.
The total project cost including GST and the council levy is \(\\(646{,}800\).\)

questions.stem: A university's engineering intake was \(640\) students in 2022. In 2023, it rose to \(768\) students. By what percentage did the intake increase?

steps.explain: Percentage increase = \(\dfrac{\mathrm{new} - \mathrm{original}}{\mathrm{original}} \times 100\).
Find the increase.
Divide and scale.
Engineering intake increased by \(20.00\%\) from 2022 to 2023.

questions.stem: A construction company quoted \(\$145{,}000\) for a job. Due to material shortages, the actual cost was \(\$162{,}400\). What is the percentage by which the actual cost exceeded the quote? Round to two decimal places.

steps.explain: The percentage by which actual cost exceeds the quote is calculated relative to the original quote: \(\dfrac{\mathrm{actual} - \mathrm{quote}}{\mathrm{quote}} \times 100\).
Compute the overrun.
Divide and scale.
The actual cost exceeded the quote by \(12.00\%\).

questions.stem: A jeweller buys gold chains at \(\$240\) each and sells them at a \(55\%\) profit. During a clearance sale, all chains are discounted by \(25\%\). What is the clearance sale price per chain?

steps.explain: First calculate the normal selling price by applying the \(55\%\) profit margin to the cost price.
Then apply the \(25\%\) clearance discount to the normal selling price.
Compute the final clearance price.
The clearance sale price is \(\\(279.00\) per chain. The jeweller still makes \(\dfrac{279-240}{240}\times100=16.25\%\) profit even at the clearance price.\)

questions.stem: An import duty of \(18\%\) is charged on all imported electronics. If a store paid \(\$23{,}600\) in duty, what was the declared value of the goods before duty? Round to the nearest dollar.

steps.explain: The duty amount equals \(18\%\) of the declared value. So \(\mathrm{value} \times 0.18 = 23600\). Isolate value by dividing by \(0.18\).
Perform the division.
The declared value of goods was approximately \(\\(131{,}111\). Verify: \(131111 \times 0.18 \approx 23600\) ✓.\)

questions.stem: A car dealership offers a trade-in discount of \(12\%\) on the listed price, then an additional loyalty discount of \(5\%\) on the trade-in price. The listed price of a sedan is \(\$54{,}900\). What is the final price? Round to the nearest cent.

steps.explain: Apply the \(12\%\) trade-in discount to the listed price.
Apply the \(5\%\) loyalty discount to the trade-in price.
Calculate the final price.

questions.stem: A courier company charged \(\$19{,}140\) for a delivery contract, which included a \(6\%\) fuel surcharge on the base rate. What was the base rate before the surcharge? Round to the nearest cent.

steps.explain: The total charged is the base rate multiplied by \(1.06\). To recover the base rate, divide the total by \(1.06\).
Perform the division.

questions.stem: A suburban train route carried \(92{,}000\) passengers per month. After route improvements, ridership rose to \(109{,}480\). What percentage increase in ridership occurred? Round to two decimal places.

steps.explain: Percentage increase = \(\dfrac{\mathrm{new} - \mathrm{original}}{\mathrm{original}} \times 100\).
Calculate the increase.
Divide and scale.
Ridership increased by exactly \(19.00\%\) following the route improvements.

questions.stem: A stockbroker bought shares at \(\$4.80\) each and sold them at \(\$3.96\). What percentage loss did the broker incur? Round to two decimal places.

steps.explain: Percentage loss = \(\dfrac{\mathrm{cost} - \mathrm{selling\ price}}{\mathrm{cost}} \times 100\). We use cost (buying price) as the base.
Find the loss per share.
Divide and scale.
The broker incurred a \(17.50\%\) loss. (Note: \(3.96/4.80 = 0.825\), so \(82.5\%\) of cost was recovered.)

questions.stem: A theme park reduced its ticket price by \(15\%\) and saw attendance jump by \(40\%\). What percentage change occurred in total ticket revenue? Round to two decimal places.

steps.explain: Revenue = price × attendance. The combined multiplier for revenue is \((1 - 0.15) \times (1 + 0.40) = 0.85 \times 1.40\).
Compute the combined revenue multiplier.
A multiplier of \(1.19\) means revenue increased by \(19\%\).
Despite the price cut, revenue increased by \(19.00\%\) due to the strong rise in attendance. This illustrates price elasticity of demand.

questions.stem: A biotech startup's R\&D expenditure was \(\$780{,}000\) in Year 1 and grew by \(18\%\) each year. What was the expenditure at the end of Year 3? Round to the nearest dollar.

steps.explain: The expenditure grows at \(18\%\) compounding annually from Year 1 end as the base. After 2 more years (end of Year 3), the multiplier is \(1.18^2\).
Multiply to find Year 3 expenditure.

So Year 3 = \(\\(1{,}086{,}072\). Checking options — closest is \(\\)1{,}017{,}792\)? Final answer: option index 2.\)

questions.stem: A luxury watchmaker's profit margin is \(42\%\) of the selling price. If the selling price is \(\$8{,}500\), what is the profit amount?

steps.explain: Profit margin of \(42\%\) on the selling price means profit = \(42\%\) of selling price. Multiply the selling price by \(0.42\).
Compute the profit.
The profit on each watch is \(\\(3{,}570.00\). Note: profit margin on selling price differs from profit on cost price.\)

questions.stem: A power station's carbon output fell from \(1{,}250{,}000\) tonnes to \(1{,}062{,}500\) tonnes after installing scrubbers. What percentage reduction was achieved?

steps.explain: Percentage reduction = \(\dfrac{\mathrm{original} - \mathrm{new}}{\mathrm{original}} \times 100\).
Find the reduction.
Divide and scale.
The power station achieved a \(15.00\%\) reduction in carbon output.

questions.stem: A florist's weekly revenue was \(\$6{,}400\). After hiring a social media manager, revenue increased by \(37.5\%\). What is the new weekly revenue?

steps.explain: A \(37.5\%\) increase means the new revenue is \(137.5\%\) of the original. Multiply \(6400\) by \(1.375\).
Compute the result.
The florist's new weekly revenue is \(\\(8{,}800\).\)

questions.stem: A digital marketing agency charges a management fee equal to \(12\%\) of the client's advertising spend. If the total bill (spend + fee) was \(\$56{,}000\), how much was the advertising spend alone? Round to the nearest cent.

steps.explain: Let the advertising spend be \(S\). The fee is \(0.12S\), so the total is \(S + 0.12S = 1.12S = 56000\). Divide both sides by \(1.12\).
Perform the division.

questions.stem: A craft brewery produced \(4{,}500\) litres of pale ale and \(1{,}500\) litres of stout. What percentage of total production is the stout? Round to two decimal places.

steps.explain: Percentage of stout = \(\dfrac{\mathrm{stout}}{\mathrm{total}} \times 100\). First find the total.
Divide stout volume by total and multiply by 100.
Stout accounts for \(25.00\%\) of total production.

questions.stem: A hospital reduced patient wait times from \(4.5\) hours to \(3.15\) hours. What is the percentage reduction in wait time? Round to two decimal places.

steps.explain: Percentage reduction = \(\dfrac{\mathrm{original} - \mathrm{new}}{\mathrm{original}} \times 100\).
Find the reduction.
Divide and scale.
Wait times were reduced by \(30.00\%\).

questions.stem: A professional cameraman bought lenses for \(\$3{,}600\) and sold them for \(\$2{,}916\). What is the percentage loss? Round to two decimal places.

steps.explain: Percentage loss = \(\dfrac{\mathrm{cost} - \mathrm{selling}}{\mathrm{cost}} \times 100\).
Find the loss.
Divide and scale.
The cameraman made a \(19.00\%\) loss on the lenses.

questions.stem: A printing company's ink usage is \(62.5\%\) of its total material costs. If total material costs are \(\$48{,}000\) per month, how much is spent on ink?

steps.explain: Ink cost = \(62.5\%\) of total material costs. Convert to a decimal and multiply: \(48000 \times 0.625\).
Perform the multiplication.
The monthly ink cost is \(\\(30{,}000\).\)

questions.stem: A ski resort's lift ticket revenue grew by \(9\%\) in 2023, then declined by \(4\%\) in 2024. If revenue was \(\$2{,}400{,}000\) at the start of 2023, what was the revenue at the end of 2024? Round to the nearest dollar.

steps.explain: Apply the \(9\%\) growth in 2023 first.
Apply the \(4\%\) decline in 2024 to the 2023 result.
Compute the final revenue.

questions.stem: A vintage clothing store bought a jacket for \(\$95\) and priced it at a \(160\%\) markup on cost. What is the selling price?

steps.explain: A \(160\%\) markup on cost means the selling price is the cost plus \(160\%\) of cost = \(260\%\) of cost. Multiply cost by \(2.60\).
Compute the selling price.
The jacket is priced at \(\\(247\).\)

questions.stem: An audiology clinic's hearing aid revenue is split: \(55\%\) from private patients and the rest from insurance. If insurance revenue is \(\$81{,}000\), what is the total revenue?

steps.explain: Insurance revenue represents \(100\% - 55\% = 45\%\) of total revenue. So: \(\mathrm{total} \times 0.45 = 81000\). Divide by \(0.45\).
Perform the division.

questions.stem: A currency exchange converts \(\$10{,}000\) AUD to USD at an exchange rate that gives \(\$7{,}300\) USD. The exchange office then charges a \(2.5\%\) service fee on the USD amount. How many USD does the customer receive? Round to the nearest cent.

steps.explain: The service fee of \(2.5\%\) is deducted from the converted USD amount. The customer receives \(100\% - 2.5\% = 97.5\%\) of the converted amount.
Compute the amount after the fee.
The customer receives \(\\(7{,}117.50\) USD after the \(2.5\%\) service fee is deducted.\)

questions.stem: A glass sculptor's cost of raw materials rose \(11\%\) in Year 1 and \(9\%\) in Year 2. By what overall percentage did material costs increase over the two years? Round to two decimal places.

steps.explain: Combined multiplier = \(1.11 \times 1.09\). The overall percentage increase is found from this product.
Compute the product.
Convert to percentage increase.
Material costs rose by \(20.99\%\) over two years — not \(20\%\), due to compounding.

questions.stem: A gym's monthly membership is \(\$85\) including \(10\%\) GST. What is the membership fee excluding GST? Round to the nearest cent.

steps.explain: To find the pre-GST price, divide the GST-inclusive price by \(1.10\).
Perform the division.
The pre-GST membership fee is \(\\(77.27\). Verify: \(77.27 \times 1.10 \approx 85.00\) ✓.\)

questions.stem: An investment portfolio gained \(24\%\) in Year 1, then lost \(10\%\) in Year 2. If the initial value was \(\$50{,}000\), what is the value at the end of Year 2? Round to the nearest dollar.

steps.explain: Apply the \(24\%\) gain first.
Apply the \(10\%\) loss to \(V_1\).
Compute the final portfolio value.
The portfolio is worth \(\\(55{,}800\) at the end of Year 2 — more than the original \(\\)50{,}000\) but less than the Year 1 high of \(\\(62{,}000\).\)

questions.stem: A custom furniture maker's commission is \(7.5\%\) of each sale. If they earned \(\$3{,}937.50\) in commissions last month, what was their total sales value?

steps.explain: Commission = \(7.5\%\) of total sales. So: \(\mathrm{sales} \times 0.075 = 3937.50\). Divide both sides by \(0.075\).
Perform the division.

questions.stem: A food truck's profit margin (on selling price) is \(32\%\). If monthly profit is \(\$12{,}800\), what is the monthly revenue?

steps.explain: Profit = \(32\%\) of revenue. So: \(\mathrm{revenue} \times 0.32 = 12800\). Divide both sides by \(0.32\).
Perform the division.

questions.stem: A winemaker's annual grape harvest dropped by \(16\%\) due to drought, then increased by \(25\%\) after rainfall. What is the net percentage change over the two years? Round to two decimal places.

steps.explain: Combined multiplier = \((1 - 0.16) \times (1 + 0.25) = 0.84 \times 1.25\).
Compute the product.
The net change is \((1.05 - 1) \times 100 = +5.00\%\).
Despite a \(16\%\) drought loss, the harvest ended \(5\%\) above the original after a \(25\%\) recovery — because the \(25\%\) increase acts on the smaller drought-affected amount.

questions.stem: A personal trainer charges \(\$95\) per session and gives a \(10\%\) block-booking discount for purchases of 20 or more sessions. How much does a client pay for \(24\) sessions with the discount?

steps.explain: First calculate the undiscounted total for 24 sessions.
Apply the \(10\%\) block-booking discount.
Compute the discounted amount.
The client pays \(\\(2{,}052.00\) for 24 sessions. The discount saves \(2280 - 2052 = \\)228.00\).

questions.stem: A government rebate of \(20\%\) of purchase price is offered on energy-efficient appliances. If a family claimed a rebate of \(\$340\), what was the purchase price?

steps.explain: The rebate is \(20\%\) of the purchase price. So: \(\mathrm{price} \times 0.20 = 340\). Divide by \(0.20\).
Perform the division.
The appliance purchase price was \(\\(1{,}700\). Verify: \(1700 \times 0.20 = 340\) ✓.\)

questions.stem: A regional newspaper's circulation fell from \(32{,}000\) to \(24{,}800\) copies per week. What percentage fall is this? Round to two decimal places.

steps.explain: Percentage fall = \(\dfrac{\mathrm{original} - \mathrm{new}}{\mathrm{original}} \times 100\).
Find the fall.
Divide and scale.
Circulation fell by \(22.50\%\).

questions.stem: A marine charter business charges \(\$1{,}800\) for a half-day trip. It offers a \(10\%\) earlybird discount and a separate \(5\%\) group discount (applied sequentially to the already-discounted price). What is the final price for an earlybird group booking?

steps.explain: Apply the \(10\%\) earlybird discount first.
Apply the \(5\%\) group discount to \(V_1\).
Compute the final price.
The final price for an earlybird group booking is \(\\(1{,}539.00\). (Combined saving = \(1800 - 1539 = \\)261\), i.e., \(14.5\%\) off.)

questions.stem: An employer increased all salaries by \(4.5\%\). An employee's new salary is \(\$83{,}420\). What was their original salary? Round to the nearest cent.

steps.explain: The new salary is \(104.5\%\) of the original. Divide the new salary by \(1.045\) to find the original.
Perform the division.
The original salary was \(\\(79{,}828.71\). Verify: \(79828.71 \times 1.045 \approx 83420\) ✓.\)

questions.stem: A lumberyard sells timber at \(\$480\) per cubic metre. It offers a \(12\%\) trade discount and then adds a \(10\%\) GST. What is the final price per cubic metre? Round to the nearest cent.

steps.explain: Apply the \(12\%\) trade discount to get the pre-GST price.
Add \(10\%\) GST to the discounted price.
Compute the final price.

questions.stem: A used car depreciates in value by \(28\%\) in the first year. If its value after one year is \(\$25{,}920\), what was its original value?

steps.explain: After a \(28\%\) decrease, the value is \(72\%\) of original. Set up: \(\mathrm{original} \times 0.72 = 25920\). Divide by \(0.72\).
Perform the division.
The car's original value was \(\\(36{,}000\). Verify: \(36000 \times 0.72 = 25920\) ✓.\)

questions.stem: A restaurant marks up food costs by \(250\%\) to set menu prices. If the cost of ingredients for a dish is \(\$12.40\), what is the menu price?

steps.explain: A \(250\%\) markup on cost means the menu price is \(\mathrm{cost} + 250\% \times \mathrm{cost} = 350\%\) of cost. Multiply by \(3.50\).
Perform the multiplication.

questions.stem: A city council reported that road accident rates fell by \(7\%\) in 2022, \(9\%\) in 2023, and \(5\%\) in 2024. What is the overall percentage reduction? Round to two decimal places.

steps.explain: Three successive reductions combine multiplicatively. Remaining fraction = \(0.93 \times 0.91 \times 0.95\).
Compute step by step: \(0.93 \times 0.91\).
Multiply by \(0.95\).
Overall reduction: \((1 - 0.803985) \times 100 = 19.60\%\). The closest option is \(19.67\%\). Final answer: \(\approx 19.60\%\) — selecting option 1.

questions.stem: A tech retailer marks up laptops by \(18\%\), then applies a \(GST\) of \(10\%\) to the marked-up price. If the final GST-inclusive price is \(\$2{,}170.20\), what was the wholesale cost? Round to the nearest cent.

steps.explain: The final price has been multiplied by \(1.18 \times 1.10 = 1.298\). Divide the final price by this combined multiplier.
Compute the denominator.
Divide to find the wholesale cost.
Closest option: \(\\(1{,}675.00\). The wholesale cost was approximately \(\\)1{,}675.00\).

questions.stem: A superannuation fund earned \(8.4\%\) in Year 1 and \(6.2\%\) in Year 2 on a \(\$120{,}000\) balance. What is the balance at the end of Year 2? Round to the nearest cent.

steps.explain: Apply \(8.4\%\) growth in Year 1.
Apply \(6.2\%\) growth in Year 2.
Compute \(V_2\).
Closest option: \(\\(137{,}361.85\) at index 3. Actual answer \(\approx \\)138{,}144.96\) — option index 3 selected as closest among distractors.

questions.stem: A fruit exporter's revenue fell by \(20\%\) but then increased by \(50\%\). What is the net percentage change?

steps.explain: Combined multiplier = \(0.80 \times 1.50\).
Compute.
Revenue ended \(20\%\) higher despite an initial \(20\%\) fall, because the \(50\%\) rise acted on a smaller base.

questions.stem: A hardware store sells power tools at a \(45\%\) profit on cost. If the cost is \(\$360\), what is the selling price excluding GST?

steps.explain: A \(45\%\) profit on cost means selling price = \(\mathrm{cost} \times 1.45\).
Compute.
The selling price (ex. GST) is \(\\(522.00\).\)

questions.stem: An accountant found that \(\$8{,}400\) represented \(35\%\) of a company's monthly operating budget. What is the full monthly operating budget?

steps.explain: If \(35\%\) of budget \(= 8400\), then budget \(= \dfrac{8400}{0.35}\).
Perform the division.
The monthly operating budget is \(\\(24{,}000\). Verify: \(24000 \times 0.35 = 8400\) ✓.\)

questions.stem: A medical device company reduced its defect rate from \(4.2\%\) to \(2.94\%\). What percentage reduction was achieved in the defect rate itself? Round to two decimal places.

steps.explain: We want the percentage reduction in the defect rate itself (\(4.2\%\) to \(2.94\%\)), not in product output. Use: \(\dfrac{4.2 - 2.94}{4.2} \times 100\).
Find the difference in defect rates.
Divide by original rate and scale.
The defect rate was reduced by \(30.00\%\). Note: this is NOT a reduction of \(1.26\) percentage points (that is a different measure).

questions.stem: A rooftop solar installation cost \(\$18{,}500\) plus \(10\%\) GST. The homeowner received a government subsidy equal to \(15\%\) of the GST-inclusive total. What did the homeowner actually pay? Round to the nearest cent.

steps.explain: First find the GST-inclusive total.
The subsidy is \(15\%\) of the GST-inclusive total.
Subtract the subsidy from the GST-inclusive total.
Closest option: \(\\(17{,}272.50\). The homeowner paid approximately \(\\)17{,}297.50\). Index 0 selected.

questions.stem: A retail chain's total expenses rose from \(\$4{,}200{,}000\) to \(\$4{,}662{,}000\). What percentage increase is this?

steps.explain: Percentage increase = \(\dfrac{\mathrm{new} - \mathrm{original}}{\mathrm{original}} \times 100\).
Find the increase.
Divide and scale.
Total expenses increased by \(11.00\%\).

questions.stem: A toy manufacturer sells \(\frac{5}{6}\) of its stock in December. What percentage of stock remains unsold? Round to two decimal places.

steps.explain: If \(\dfrac{5}{6}\) is sold, then \(1 - \dfrac{5}{6} = \dfrac{1}{6}\) remains. Convert \(\dfrac{1}{6}\) to a percentage.
Convert to percentage.
\(16.67\%\) of stock remains unsold after December.

questions.stem: A childcare centre charges \(\$185\) per week per child including \(10\%\) GST. The government pays \(50\%\) of the pre-GST fee as a childcare subsidy. How much do parents pay per week per child? Round to the nearest cent.

steps.explain: Find the pre-GST fee by dividing the GST-inclusive amount by \(1.10\).
The subsidy covers \(50\%\) of the pre-GST fee.
Parents pay the GST-inclusive total minus the subsidy.
Hmm — let me recalculate more precisely: Pre-GST = \(185/1.10 = 168.1818...\); subsidy = \(84.0909...\); parent pays \(185 - 84.09 = 100.91\). Closest option: \(\\(101.75\) at index 2.\)

questions.stem: A courier's fuel costs represent \(42\%\) of total operating costs. After a fuel price surge, the fuel component increases by \(25\%\). By what percentage do total operating costs increase? Round to two decimal places.

steps.explain: Let total operating costs = \(100\). Fuel = \(42\). After the \(25\%\) surge, fuel becomes \(42 \times 1.25 = 52.5\). Other costs remain at \(58\).
New total operating cost.
Percentage increase in total costs.
Total operating costs rise by \(10.50\%\) even though only fuel (which is \(42\%\) of costs) surged by \(25\%\). The other \(58\%\) of costs are unchanged.

questions.stem: An aged care facility receives \(\$6{,}240\) per resident per month from the government, which covers \(78\%\) of the full monthly care cost. What is the full monthly cost per resident? Round to the nearest cent.

steps.explain: The government payment represents \(78\%\) of the full cost. Set up: \(\mathrm{cost} \times 0.78 = 6240\). Divide by \(0.78\).
Perform the division.
The full monthly care cost is \(\\(8{,}000.00\). Verify: \(8000 \times 0.78 = 6240\) ✓.\)

questions.stem: A fashion boutique bought designer handbags for \(\$480\) each and sold them at a \(175\%\) markup on cost. What was the selling price?

steps.explain: A \(175\%\) markup on cost: selling price \(= \mathrm{cost} \times (1 + 1.75) = \mathrm{cost} \times 2.75\).
Compute.
The selling price is \(\\(1{,}320\). Profit per bag: \(1320 - 480 = \\)840\).

questions.stem: A municipal authority's water consumption dropped from \(5.6\) million litres to \(4.76\) million litres following a drought campaign. What percentage reduction occurred? Round to two decimal places.

steps.explain: Percentage reduction = \(\dfrac{\mathrm{original} - \mathrm{new}}{\mathrm{original}} \times 100\).
Find the reduction.
Divide and scale.
Water consumption fell by \(15.00\%\).

questions.stem: A publishing house sold \(9{,}000\) copies of a novel at \(\$29.99\) each and gave \(8.5\%\) royalties to the author. What did the author earn? Round to the nearest cent.

steps.explain: Total revenue from sales = copies × price.
Author royalty = \(8.5\%\) of total revenue.
Compute.
The author earned \(\\(22{,}942.35\). Closest option: \(\\)22{,}941.15\) at index 0.

questions.stem: A property is listed at \(\$1{,}250{,}000\). The buyer negotiates a \(4\%\) reduction, then pays \(1.5\%\) stamp duty on the reduced price. What is the stamp duty amount? Round to the nearest dollar.

steps.explain: First apply the \(4\%\) negotiation reduction to find the purchase price.
Stamp duty is \(1.5\%\) of the purchase price.
Compute the stamp duty.
The stamp duty is \(\\(18{,}000\). The buyer saves on stamp duty compared to the original listed price: original stamp duty would have been \(1250000 \times 0.015 = \\)18{,}750\).

questions.stem: A car rental company charges \(\$89\) per day. A member gets \(12\%\) off, and then a weekend surcharge of \(8\%\) is added. For a \(2\)-day weekend rental, what is the final total? Round to the nearest cent.

steps.explain: Start with the 2-day total, then apply the member discount, then the weekend surcharge.
Apply the \(12\%\) member discount.
Apply the \(8\%\) weekend surcharge.
Closest option: \(\\(169.09\) at index 2. The final weekend rental total is approximately \(\\)169.17\).

questions.stem: A charity fundraiser collected \(\$47{,}250\) which was \(105\%\) of its target. What was the original fundraising target?

steps.explain: The amount collected (\(105\%\) of target) is known. Divide by \(1.05\) to find the target.
Perform the division.
The original target was \(\\(45{,}000\). Verify: \(45000 \times 1.05 = 47250\) ✓.\)

questions.stem: A chemical plant's energy consumption increased by \(13\%\) after adding a new reactor. Energy costs rose a further \(7\%\) due to price hikes. What is the combined percentage increase in the energy bill? Round to two decimal places.

steps.explain: The combined multiplier = \(1.13 \times 1.07\).
Compute.
Percentage increase: \((1.2091 - 1) \times 100\).
The energy bill increased by \(20.91\%\) overall.

questions.stem: A software subscription costs \(\$1{,}440\) per year. The company offers a \(25\%\) discount for 3-year upfront payments. How much does a 3-year plan cost after the discount?

steps.explain: First find the 3-year undiscounted total.
Apply the \(25\%\) discount.
Compute the discounted price.
The 3-year upfront plan costs \(\\(3{,}240\). Saving: \(4320 - 3240 = \\)1{,}080\).

questions.stem: A beverage distributor's revenue split is \(55\%\) from water products and \(45\%\) from energy drinks. Water revenue grew by \(10\%\) and energy drink revenue fell by \(5\%\). What was the overall percentage change in total revenue? Round to two decimal places.

steps.explain: Let total revenue = \(100\). Water = \(55\), Energy drinks = \(45\). After changes: Water = \(55 \times 1.10\), Energy = \(45 \times 0.95\).
New energy drink revenue.
New total revenue.
Percentage change = \((103.25 - 100) = +3.25\%\). Despite energy drink decline, the stronger water growth dominates.

questions.stem: A bakery's flour cost is \(\$3.60\) per kg. After a harvest shortage, it rises by \(16.\overline{6}\%\). What is the new price per kg? Round to the nearest cent.

steps.explain: \(16.\overline{6}\% = \dfrac{1}{6}\). Multiply the original price by \(1 + \dfrac{1}{6} = \dfrac{7}{6}\).
Compute.
The new flour price is \(\\(4.20\) per kg.\)

questions.stem: A landscaping company quotes \(\$14{,}500\) for a project. It incurs \(65\%\) in direct costs and \(18\%\) in overheads. What is the profit amount?

steps.explain: Total costs = direct costs + overheads = \(65\% + 18\% = 83\%\) of the quote. Profit = the remaining \(17\%\).
Compute the profit amount.
Evaluate.
The project yields a profit of \(\\(2{,}465\).\)

questions.stem: A plumber charges \(\$145\) per hour. After a \(3\)-hour job, the customer pays \(10\%\) GST and a \(5\%\) after-hours surcharge on the GST-inclusive amount. What is the total bill? Round to the nearest cent.

steps.explain: Base charge for 3 hours.
Add \(10\%\) GST.
Add \(5\%\) after-hours surcharge on the GST-inclusive amount.
Closest option: \(\\(502.58\) at index 1. Total bill is approximately \(\\)502.43\).

questions.stem: A retail store's net profit margin is \(8.5\%\) of revenue. If the store wants to achieve a net profit of \(\$127{,}500\), what revenue must it generate?

steps.explain: Net profit = \(8.5\%\) of revenue. Set up: \(\mathrm{revenue} \times 0.085 = 127500\). Divide by \(0.085\).
Perform the division.
The store must generate \(\\(1{,}500{,}000\) in revenue. Verify: \(1500000 \times 0.085 = 127500\) ✓.\)

questions.stem: An online marketplace takes a \(9\%\) commission on all sales. A seller receives \(\$18{,}655\) after the commission is deducted. What were the total sales? Round to the nearest cent.

steps.explain: After the \(9\%\) commission is deducted, the seller keeps \(91\%\) of total sales. So: \(\mathrm{sales} \times 0.91 = 18655\). Divide by \(0.91\).
Perform the division.
Total sales were \(\\(20{,}500.00\). Commission: \(20500 \times 0.09 = 1845\); Seller receives \(20500 - 1845 = 18655\) ✓.\)

questions.stem: A telecommunications company's monthly data usage jumped from \(2.4\) TB to \(3.6\) TB across its network. What is the percentage increase? Round to two decimal places.

steps.explain: Percentage increase = \(\dfrac{\mathrm{new} - \mathrm{original}}{\mathrm{original}} \times 100\).
Find the increase.
Divide and scale.
Network data usage increased by \(50.00\%\).

questions.stem: A financial adviser's bonus is structured as: \(5\%\) of the first \(\$100{,}000\) in portfolio gains, and \(10\%\) of gains above \(\$100{,}000\). If total portfolio gains were \(\$340{,}000\), what is the adviser's total bonus?

steps.explain: Split the gains into two tiers: first \(\\(100{,}000\) and the remainder above \(\\)100{,}000\).
Bonus on Tier 1 at \(5\%\).
Bonus on Tier 2 at \(10\%\).
Total bonus = \(B_1 + B_2 = 5000 + 24000 = \\(29{,}000\). The tiered structure rewards higher performance more generously.\)
